title: [Chapitre] II. Réalisations topologiques des réseaux : notes manuscrites (06/06/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
Context (from p.4): a 'ficelle' (string) is a pair (X,{A,B}) of a space X and two disjoint closed subsets A, B, its 'ends'. Collapsing A and B to points a, b gives X'. The conditions are labelled a)–d). From this page and the previous one they seem to say: X is connected; the ends are not isolated; X'∖{a} and X'∖{b} are connected; and d) some local irreducibility or local connectedness condition at the ends. A 'lieu/lien' (link) C is a closed subset C ⊂ X∖(A∪B) such that X∖C splits uniquely into two disjoint open sets U_{A,C} ⊃ A and U_{B,C} ⊃ B, with U_{A,C}/A and U_{B,C}/B connected.

This page: set X_{A,C} = closure(U_{A,C}) ∪ C, and similarly X_{B,C}. The claim is that (X_{A,C},{A,C}) again satisfies conditions a), b), c) of a string; by symmetry so does (X_{B,C},{B,C}). So cutting a string at a link gives two sub-strings. This is the first step towards decomposing a string into a chain of links (p.6: 'décomposition de la ficelle en liens').

Proof. Collapse A, B, C to points a, b, c.
- Since U_{a,c} and U_{b,c} are open and disjoint with union X∖{c}, the boundary of U_{a,c} lies in {c}. Hence X_{a,c} = U_{a,c} ∪ {c}.
- a is not isolated in X_{a,c}: it is not isolated in X, and X_{a,c} is a neighbourhood of a.
- c is not isolated in X_{a,c}: otherwise U_{a,c} would be closed as well as open in X, and X would be disconnected.
- X_{a,c}∖{c} = U_{a,c} is connected by hypothesis.
- X_{a,c}∖{a} is connected. Otherwise it contains a nonempty clopen V not containing c (if a clopen set contains c, take its complement). Then V ⊂ U_{a,c}∖{a} is open in X. V is also closed in X∖{a}, because X_{a,c}∖{a} is closed in X∖{a}. Its complement in X∖{a} contains c, so it is nonempty. Hence X∖{a} is disconnected, contradicting the string hypothesis.

What remains is condition d), local irreducibility at the new end C. The next page handles it with a gluing lemma: for closed Z', Z'' with Z'∩Z'' = {c}, c has a connected neighbourhood in Z' ∪ Z'' iff it has one in each piece.
errors: The conclusion as written reads 'donc X∖{c} ne serait pas connexe'. The argument actually gives that X∖{a} is not connected: V is clopen in X∖{a}, and its complement there contains c. This is a slip of letter or a transcription issue.

The reduction to the case where A, B, C are points (passing to quotient spaces) is asserted without justification. It needs mild separation or compactness hypotheses to ensure openness, closedness and connectedness transfer through the quotient.
The proof that a is not isolated is only sketched in an interlinear insertion. It is correct, since X_{a,c} ⊃ U_{a,c} ∋ a and U_{a,c} is open in X.

ideas.what: Strings (ficelles): spaces with two closed 'ends' A, B, with connectedness conditions on the complements of each end. A topological axiomatization of 'arc-like' edges for topological realizations of networks.
ideas.modern_name: Continua irreducible between two points/sets; arc characterizations via non-cut points
ideas.usually_credited_to: R. L. Moore, Kline, Whyburn, Kuratowski (continuum theory, 1920s–40s)

ideas.what: Cutting a string at a separating closed set (link) C gives two sub-strings (X_{A,C},{A,C}) and (X_{B,C},{B,C}).
ideas.modern_name: Separation order / subdivision of irreducible continua at cut sets

ideas.what: Local connectedness at a one-point gluing (lemma on the next page) as the remaining condition d).
ideas.modern_name: Local connectedness of wedge/gluing along a point

deep.surprise_reason: Elementary point-set topology verifying that cutting a string at a link yields two sub-strings. It is correct apart from a letter slip and is standard in continuum theory. Its only interest is as a step in Grothendieck's 1986 program on topological realizations of networks.
transcription_corrections: Line 1: the page begins 'NB Soit X_{A,C} = \overline{U_{A,C}} ∪ C'. The first subscript in the image is written 'A,C' with a bold C.
The interlinear insertion reads approximately: 'Il faut prouver que a n'est pas isolé dans X_{a,c} puisqu'il ne l'est pas dans X et X_{a,c} est un voisinage de a dans X (?)'.
'serait non connexe, absurde' is preceded by the corrected 'serait' replacing 'On aurait'; the reading is 'U_{ac} serait ouvert et fermé dans X, X serait non connexe, absurde'.

'Il ne manque que l'hypothèse d), d'irréductibilité locale' — the transcription is plausible. The last word may be 'locale' or 'locale.' and the preceding word may be 'd'irréductibilité' or 'd'impénétrabilité'; 'irréductibilité' is the best reading in context.
